contexts.description: Quality gates for a drafted article. It runs deterministic prose, static and rendered checks in a check loop. A multi-model critique then reviews the draft, and its reviews are written back for the next draft. Reports feed the human gate.
contexts.name: article-check-and-critique

contexts.api_surface: Board packet pkt:article:<runId>; opens PR in ai-registry
contexts.description: Handles the human approval gate and the landing of an approved article. Human acts and notes are recorded, diffs are produced for the Board, and a Medium package is built. Approval writes the post into ai-registry via a PR, which puts the run's blog slot on the Calendar. Registry read and write adapters and run file helpers live here.
contexts.name: article-human-gate-and-landing

contexts.api_surface: CLI pipeline/article.mts (run, status)
contexts.description: Drives a technical blog post from a registry topic through research, outline and draft steps. It manages run creation, persisted run state, agent turns, resume, rework and step-failure handling. Agent output is ingested from drafts and sources, and a dry stand-in agent replaces the real Claude seat for rehearsals.
contexts.name: article-run-engine

contexts.description: The Library screen: tiles, rows, faces, rail, detail panel, lineage and set summaries for browsing generated assets. library.ts models the selection and grouping that the Library's feeds supply.
contexts.name: asset-library-browser

contexts.api_surface: Library query, counts, detail, write
contexts.description: The Library's kernel side: asset schema, write path, queries with clause builders, counts, detail and measures. Serves the Library screens from the kernel store.
contexts.name: asset-library-store

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST app/(studio)/audio/return route handler
contexts.description: The audio studio route where tracks are arranged, played back and dragged into lanes. The page reads through the route's port, and the Arrange and AudioLane components drive card drag, transport and desk actions. The return route receives results coming back from the audio vendor flow.
contexts.name: audio-arrange-desk

contexts.description: Authoring side of the audio studio: prompts, seeds, briefs and their deltas, batch forms, engine and draft lists, references and variations. Each form pairs with a pure model (brief.ts, batch.ts, recipe.ts, variations.ts) so state is data. Output goes to the audio producers through the route port.
contexts.name: audio-composer-briefs

contexts.api_surface: audio hunt-return route handler
contexts.description: The Hunt tab of the audio studio, where candidate tracks are searched for and judged. Hunt.tsx renders what the read layer returns and the acts send decisions. The leaf return and its route bring results back and set the URL state.
contexts.name: audio-hunt

contexts.description: The audio studio's hunt and arrange surfaces: auditioning takes, mapping the hunt, rendering, and arranging takes into groups. Pure models (hunt.ts, arrange.ts, arrangeGroups.ts) feed the React boards that the audio route reads through its port. Depends on the Wave and Chip primitives for waveform and verdict display.
contexts.name: audio-hunt-arrange

contexts.description: Insight and Lessons tabs of the audio studio. They show the batch, the rubric and the strengths of generated music, and the lessons drawn from past judgements. Each reads through its own port and sends acts back.
contexts.name: audio-insight-lessons

contexts.description: Judging and learning for generated audio: measures, rubric scoring, strengths, previews, and lessons recorded from takes. Pure models (rubric.ts, strengths.ts, lesson.ts, audio.ts) back the lists and forms.
contexts.name: audio-lessons-measures

contexts.api_surface: Producer set consumed by lib/producers and the Board
contexts.description: Producers for audio, script and text work plus the producer registry: music video plan, score, Suno, voice, words, script, article, dojo, forge and the top-level set. Each defines a plan or producer that the kernel prices through receipts and runs, with JSON case fixtures for plans. The set aggregates all producers for the layers above.
contexts.name: audio-text-producers

contexts.api_surface: Server-only module: adapterFor(source) and the apply-outbox drain consumed by the Board route
contexts.description: Adapts each v1 store (dojo, forge, extract, strips, articles, audio, music video, proof, suno) into Board decision packets and applies the operator's verdicts back to those stores. A registry maps a packet source to its adapter, and the applier drains the kernel's apply outbox through that adapter under a lease. Reject reasons carried in free-text notes are encoded and decoded in note.ts. Depends on @gt/domain, @gt/kernel and the v1 stores.
contexts.name: board-decision-adapters

contexts.api_surface: POST /board/[packet]/keepalive (sendBeacon verdict flush); Board Server Actions via _port/actions.ts
contexts.description: The Board is the studio's decision surface. An operator opens one packet on a level sheet, with a rail of every packet beside it, then rules on verdicts, picks, undos and commits, and reviews what was decided and what was lost. The client island (Board, DecidedDesk, Losses, commitFlow) talks only to a BoardPort. The port is the seam, switched by GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE between a fixture and the real kernel decision driver, with server actions, a wire envelope, packet-param parsing and a keepalive beacon route that flushes queued verdicts on pagehide. Legacy v1 board addresses redirect to the packet or Floor lane they became.
contexts.name: board-decision-desk

contexts.api_surface: Producer registry consumed by the kernel job worker; calls vendor APIs (LLM, image, music, speech) through metered calls with a dry-run default
contexts.description: Binds the pure producer definitions in @gt/producers to the v1 stores and vendors, so each production step (article, research, script, words, voice, sound, suno, still, frames, motion, cut, strips, style, extract, forge, score, dojo, music-video, publish, media-facts) runs as a kernel job. Each file builds a Producer: it plans and prices a receipt, takes a resource lane, runs metered calls, and returns step outcomes and events. registry.ts maps producer names to these implementations for the job worker.
contexts.name: bound-producers

contexts.api_surface: Decision apply/commit/read, part gate checks
contexts.description: Human decisions on Board packets: schema, view, apply, commit, consequence and driver, with the pure core separated from persistence. Also the kernel's part gates and part driver, which hold production parts at their gates.
contexts.name: decision-and-gates

contexts.api_surface: Exports consumed as @gt/domain/* across kernel, producers and UI
contexts.description: Core domain primitives: branded ids, AppError types, the zod door through which all external data enters, plus the Board's decision, packet and event models and source definitions. Packets follow a state machine and decisions are recorded as events.
contexts.name: domain-decision-board-core

contexts.api_surface: Exports consumed as @gt/domain/* by studio routes
contexts.description: Domain types and state machines for parts (album, data, finish, frames views), projects, content slots and publications. Part views project the underlying records into the shapes the studio screens render.
contexts.name: domain-parts-projects-slots

contexts.api_surface: Exports consumed as @gt/domain/* by kernel, producers and studio routes
contexts.description: Domain model for production runs: the run and job state machines, lane capacity, plans, cost estimates, produce schemas, and the per-step definitions (research, script, still, frames, parts, record, finish). Transitions are expressed as data and validated with zod; steps are collected in a registry the kernel and producers consume.
contexts.name: domain-run-job-steps

contexts.api_surface: Exports consumed as @gt/domain/* by library screens and producers
contexts.description: Domain model for visual styles (with their state machine and ratchet), library items, candidates and blobs. Styles are curated and locked through a ratchet, and library items and candidates reference stored blobs.
contexts.name: domain-style-library-assets

contexts.api_surface: Server actions for scheduling; calendar port read/write contract
contexts.description: The Calendar's data port for the Floor. It selects fixture or real data according to GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE and defines the wire contract, the readiness checks and the schedule actions. The real side reads the stores that hold scheduled work and slots.
contexts.name: floor-calendar-port

contexts.description: The Floor's publishing calendar: month and column views, slot rows and details, the schedule form and slot confirmation. Pure date and slot models (calendar.ts, schedule.ts, slot.ts) drive the views and the scheduling flow that lands runs on channels.
contexts.name: floor-calendar-slots

contexts.api_surface: GET /floor?lane=&cal=&day= (server-rendered page)
contexts.description: The studio's /floor hub: four media lanes flowing from the Foundry (running work) through the Weir (piles waiting on the operator) to the Library/Projects column, plus the Calendar rail that opens into a month view. A Server Component (page.tsx, load.ts) reads the stores and hands the data to one client island. The focused lane and the open month travel in search params so links can carry them.
contexts.name: floor-hub-screen

contexts.description: The Floor's lane view of work in flight: lanes, piles, run rows, shelf cells and channel readiness. floor.ts holds the shared model; the glyphs give each lane its mark.
contexts.name: floor-lanes-runs

contexts.api_surface: Driven by lib/producers/extract.ts kernel job; CLI pipeline/foundry/extract.mts; reads foundry-out/extract/<id>/run.json
contexts.description: The Extract module that derives reusable art styles from a gallery of images. A resumable step machine runs one bounded unit per call (read, group, replicate with self-critique, transfer onto neutral scenes, finish), keeping the manifest as its only state. It carries its own prompts, spend accounting, circuit breaker, journal, vocabulary and disk layer, and runs on a laptop CLI or a request-bound host.
contexts.name: foundry-extract-engine

contexts.api_surface: Consumed by /foundry-era API routes and the ledger v1 projection; reads foundry-out/runs/<id>/run.json and writes verdicts.json
contexts.description: The Foundry's server-side core: the forge run store, the shared run-store kernel and fs port, the verdict log and commit planning behind the human cull. It also holds the style catalogue door onto the kernel store, adoption of proven styles into Library themes, grader-vs-human calibration, and the plant-state projection. Runs are read from foundry-out via the fs port and committed through planned, tokenised operations.
contexts.name: foundry-forge-store-and-verdicts

contexts.api_surface: /api/foundry/strips/* routes; Dojo gate on the Board
contexts.description: The Strips authoring and triage lane plus the Dojo training loop's disk layer. Strips runs an agent turn in an isolated workspace to author a strip, then lints, renders cards and steps, and records the operator's triage and commit plan. Training holds the cycle store and the blind A/B/tie gate that keeps judge picks hidden from the human verdict.
contexts.name: foundry-strips-and-training

contexts.api_surface: Pure library consumed by the Frames step hooks (app/_phases/frames/useFrames.ts), Score picture spotting and the Board alternatives source; no HTTP routes
contexts.description: Models the Frames step: a composed picture as plate, vector elements and texts, so facts are drawn by code and only feel is left to a model. It validates the scene-direction engine's output into frames, turns the direction pass into a per-beat proposal that can be accepted or reverted, and derives one-to-many shots per beat with their text-to-image prompts and review findings. The persisted frames record migrates from v1 to v2 picture units, which Score, Cut and the Board read.
contexts.name: frames-picture-composition

contexts.api_surface: Image generation and pricing handlers consumed by app routes and producers
contexts.description: Entry layer for image generation: request handlers, the router that picks a vendor, and the pricing, budget, forecast and receipt logic that prices every job before it runs. Shared plumbing (env, http, json, log, safe-URL checks, typed errors) keeps vendor calls bounded and dry-run by default. Providers and video clips plug in underneath.
contexts.name: imaging-gateway-and-spend

contexts.api_surface: Outbound vendor APIs (Leonardo, Google, Ollama, Qwen) and Leonardo Studio browser automation
contexts.description: Vendor adapters for image generation (Google, Leonardo, Ollama, Qwen, agy) including a browser-driven Leonardo Studio driver with selectors and a fake for tests, plus the Leonardo video clip pipeline with its own store, pricing and budget. The router in the gateway selects among these; each call is priced and receipted before spend.
contexts.name: imaging-vendor-providers-and-video

contexts.api_surface: Job enqueue, claim, run, settle
contexts.description: Durable vendor-job execution: queueing, worker loop, run and settle steps, leases that keep two workers off one job, and crash/process handling. Dry-run and effects modules keep rehearsals from spending. Pure cores are split from the store-bound drivers.
contexts.name: job-queue-and-leases

contexts.api_surface: CLI: python job.py status <store> <job-id>; python lease.py status <store> <resource>; python verify_events.py <store> [--anchor SEQ:HASH]; line-protocol spec servers job_spec.py, lease_spec.py, styles_spec.py
contexts.description: The Python implementation of the kernel's SQLite-backed protocols, so Python workers (forge, Dojo, acquire) share one job queue, GPU lease, hash-chained event ledger, spend meter, style store and project-release path with the Node kernel. Each module mirrors a TypeScript counterpart in packages/kernel/src over the same tables, using only the standard library. The `*_spec.py` and `lease_contend.py` files are the Python half of the cross-language spec and mixed-process tests that hold both languages to the same behaviour.
contexts.name: kernel-python-protocol

contexts.api_surface: Kernel open/store handle, event append and query
contexts.description: The SQLite-backed kernel store: connection, migrations, canonical hashing, blobs, tokens and ingest, plus the append-only event log with count and query readers. Every other kernel module writes and reads through this seam. Depends on @gt/domain and zod.
contexts.name: kernel-store-and-events

contexts.api_surface: GET /kit
contexts.description: The /kit route page, section index and navigation, plus specimens for the foundational vocabulary: tokens, controls, status, signal, motion, structure, spec and contract. Tokens are read from packages/ui/tokens/source.json and the status table, so the page shows the design system as shipped.
contexts.name: kit-design-system-specimens

contexts.description: Specimen cards on /kit for the studio's screens: Audio, Board, Floor, Ledger, Library, Part, Produce, Runs and Style kits, with the fixture data behind the Board and Produce specimens. Each kit renders the @gt/ui components for that screen in every state so the design system can be checked against the real surfaces.
contexts.name: kit-screen-specimens

contexts.description: The paper-texture and rasterisation side of the landing cosmos: paper and ream layout, ink and palette definitions, seeded RNG, and the raster pipeline that paints off the main thread via a worker and job queue. Keeps the visuals deterministic and the main thread free.
contexts.name: landing-cosmos-paper-raster

contexts.description: Scene composition and animation for the landing cosmos: scene specs and painting, worlds, dioramas, motifs, ambient life, camera and depth planes, plus the banner, carousel, library and medal layers shown on the page. Specs are declared as data and painted onto layers that the camera moves through.
contexts.name: landing-cosmos-scenes

contexts.description: The public landing page's React shell and the engine's orchestration layer. Cosmos.tsx mounts the canvas/DOM stage, wires the page parts, fonts, copy data and styles, and the engine modules drive state, navigation, tabs, search, keyboard control, the intro sequence and performance throttling. Consumed by app/page.tsx.
contexts.name: landing-cosmos-shell

contexts.api_surface: Server Actions olderEvents, relatedEvents; consumes /api/events/stream (SSE)
contexts.description: The /ledger studio screen: every act the studio knows as one typed, append-only list. The server component reads the kernel event store through a single bounded read module (keyset pagination, facet counts with each facet excluding its own filter, per-day strip counts), with URL search params as the filter; the client half handles typing, selection, the detail drawer and a live fetch-based SSE edge that triggers coalesced refreshes. Depends on @gt/kernel events-query/count, @gt/ui components, and the v1 ledger projection sync.
contexts.name: ledger-screen

contexts.api_surface: Consumed by the Ledger and Runs screens, the sync CLI and tests
contexts.description: Defines the v1 Ledger projection contract: the Source interface, event types, facts and packet shapes. The sync reads each source's v1 store through its adapters and projects pure events into the kernel store. The Ledger and Runs screens build on this contract, and it depends on @gt/domain event, job and lane types.
contexts.name: ledger-v1-projection-core

contexts.api_surface: Implements the Source interface from lib/ledger/v1/types.ts
contexts.description: Per-store adapters that read v1 stores (articles, clips, extract, forge, gpu, music video, publish, sound, spend, strips, suno, training, turns) and project them into ledger events, live in-flight work and independent tallies. Each is a pure projection over v1's own readers and never writes to a v1 store. Roots resolves store locations.
contexts.name: ledger-v1-sources

contexts.api_surface: GET /library/fixture-tone
contexts.description: The Library route of the studio, where the operator browses, filters and inspects produced assets. A toolbar, URL-synced query state, a results grid and a detail view are composed in Library.tsx, with a narrow-viewport hook and block helpers. The route page reads through the library port, and a fixture-tone route serves a stand-in audio tone for the fixture side.
contexts.name: library-browser-screen

contexts.api_surface: Library port contract; server actions
contexts.description: The data seam for the Library screen. A contract and port select between fixture data (corpus and data files) and the real side, which is chosen by GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE. Wire, present and handoff modules shape records for display and for passing to other screens, and actions hold the server-side mutations.
contexts.name: library-port

contexts.api_surface: Serves blob addresses at /api/blob/[sha]?type=; the Library routes read the kernel index that these feeds fill.
contexts.description: Builds the Library's searchable index of everything the studio has made. Each feed (foundry styles, forge, extract, dojo and strips; sound suno, takes, registry and music-video; studio clips and exports; kernel items) is read, its file media is ingested into blobs, and its items are upserted into the kernel Library index. Feeds that no longer hold an item are pruned, and new media is probed for facts. It also holds the seeded 50k fixture corpus, the p95 latency probe that measures it, the style trial set, and the media route helpers.
contexts.name: library-projection-feeds

contexts.description: Turns finished tracks into music videos: imports folders, fetches audio, plans sections and treatments, picks looks, composites and renders, and writes YouTube metadata. Steps, queue and store track each track's job; the compositor is the render core.
contexts.name: music-video-pipeline

contexts.description: Holds the shipped research notebook fixture (facts, unknowns, conclusions) and the derived views the review board draws from it. The notebook source, flattened cards, review dimensions and counts keep research Step 1 and the Step 2 impact matrix reading the same notebook. Growth lands in the facts file, while counts are computed over whichever notebook is active.
contexts.name: notebook-content-and-board

contexts.description: Defines the research notebook contract (types, JSON schema, snake_case dialect) and the runtime door that decides whether a model's answer counts as a notebook. Validation is split into shape, graph and retrieval halves, with a typed failure for answers that are not notebooks. Shared by the research and script steps, the corpus probe and the check-notebook gate.
contexts.name: notebook-contract-validation

contexts.api_surface: Consumes the part port for frames, cut, score and render reads and actions
contexts.business_feature: Part Editing: Frames, Cut and Score
contexts.description: Editors for the media-side parts of a project: frames and their inspector, motion, the cut with its clock and finish step, score with beds, fields and takes, voice, trailer and render. These screens let an operator review and steer generated picture, sound and edit decisions. They read through the part port and render @gt/ui components.
contexts.name: part-editor-media-cut-score

contexts.api_surface: Consumes the part port (server actions) for reading and saving part content
contexts.description: Editors for the text-side parts of a project: scripts, articles, ads briefs, scenarios, beats, research notebooks, findings and word-level editing. PartEditor dispatches to the right editor by part kind and shares styling through Editors.module.css. Reads and writes through the part port and renders @gt/ui components.
contexts.name: part-editor-writing-research

contexts.description: Fixture-side data for the part editors, used when GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE=fixture: sample acts, ads, album, cut, explainer, frames, motion, research, score and script content. Lets every part screen render deterministically without touching the store or spending on vendors.
contexts.name: part-port-fixtures

contexts.api_surface: Server actions for part edits; reads kernel records via the real port
contexts.description: The per-project part page and the port that feeds the part editors: contract, schema, wire format, kinds, hashing and server actions. The real side reads kernel records for scripts, research, scenes and recommendations, and the port picks fixture or real by GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE. View modules shape research and script records for the screens.
contexts.name: part-port-real-and-contract

contexts.description: The part workspace and Board desk: tabs, frame canvas, rail list and verdict chips for a film part, plus the desk with its packet rail and plates. part.ts models the workspace state.
contexts.name: part-workspace-desk

contexts.api_surface: Calls /api/import
contexts.description: The plan view of a project (composition list, summary, receipt and empty state) and the import flow that brings external material into a project. The plan shows what a launch will compose and cost before spend; import wraps the /api/import door.
contexts.name: plan-and-import

contexts.description: Composing a vendor job and pricing it: compose dialog, composer, plan table, lane holds, reroutes, unpriced items and the receipt. produce.ts models the plan so every job is priced through a receipt before it runs.
contexts.name: produce-compose-receipt

contexts.api_surface: Module API: readStep, loadStep, saveStep, patchStep, onSaveIssued, onStorageTrouble, SCHEMA_VERSION
contexts.description: Per-project persistence of each pipeline step's content (research, script, cut, score, music-video source) in IndexedDB, keyed by `${projectId}:${phase}`, so opening a step in one project never shows another's data. It provides an honest read path that separates never-written from failed, latest-wins and issue-ordered writes, atomic read-modify-write patching, schema-version stamping and a record registry that refuses to downgrade newer records. Storage failures and successes are published through trouble and ok channels that surfaces subscribe to. Depends on lib/studioDb and the project seed.
contexts.name: project-step-store

contexts.api_surface: Server actions for launching and rerouting projects
contexts.description: The Projects list and new-project pages together with the port that serves them: contract, wire, schedule, fixture and real reads, launching a project, choices and rerouting. Real side reads kernel stores and launches producer jobs; fixture side serves canned data.
contexts.name: projects-index-port

contexts.api_surface: Publish adapter interface; tick and timer hooks consumed by workers/
contexts.description: Publishing producers that push finished work to platforms and track how it performs. An adapter, mode and wire layer feeds a publish step, a standing check, a tick and timers, and metrics collection. It sits above the kernel job model and is driven by the worker's publish tick and metrics timers.
contexts.name: publish-producers

contexts.api_surface: Producer definitions registered with the kernel
contexts.description: Research producers that gather and meter facts for a piece, including the media-facts core. Covers fact collection, follow-up questions, metered spend, and the part-level act and job definitions. Results feed script and article producers.
contexts.name: research-producers

contexts.description: Board packet review and run history: approve-schedule, article page, packet review, plus the runs day line, lane chips and resource summary. Pure models (runs/dayline, lanes, thread, review/schedule) shape what the operator approves and what a day of runs looked like.
contexts.name: review-and-runs-history

contexts.api_surface: Run launch/read/write, slot import/outcome/sweep
contexts.description: Run records (launch, plan, schedule, reroute, receipts, options) and publishing slots (import, outcome, sweep). Records capture what ran and why, slots hold scheduled outputs on the calendar. Both use schema/read/write splits over the kernel store.
contexts.name: run-records-and-slots

contexts.api_surface: Consumes /api/events/stream
contexts.description: The Runs screen listing kernel jobs with an inspector, acts, music-video acts and dojo doors. Model, view and load modules shape job records, a live feed follows running jobs, and read keys scope what each run exposes.
contexts.name: runs-console

contexts.api_surface: Consumed by /api/script and lib/producers/script.ts
contexts.description: Composes, validates and versions the film script from notebook cards. It assembles the compose prompt, parses the model's answer through a zod door, checks constraints and scope conflicts, and gates edits with impact analysis, recalibration and render tracking. It is shared by the script API route and the kernel script producer, and depends on the notebook library.
contexts.name: script-composition-and-validation

contexts.api_surface: Vendor audio-generation HTTP clients; sound CLI
contexts.description: Generates music and sound-effect takes through vendor engines, arranges and edits them, and persists takes with spend booked on the ledger. A CLI, HTTP client and batch runner drive engine adapters; takes land in the sound store with typed records. Depends on the kernel spend ledger and vendor APIs.
contexts.name: sound-generation-engine

contexts.description: Hunts for acceptable sound takes and measures them against a rubric, turning outcomes into lessons, insights and triage order. Hunt engine and desk drive candidate searches; measure runs score audio; knowledge and vocabulary carry the accumulated music-prompt learning.
contexts.name: sound-hunt-and-measure

contexts.api_surface: Quote, meter and settle vendor spend
contexts.description: Spend control: price quotes and receipts from the pricing table, plus the spend ledger, meter, projection and settler that enforce budgets before any vendor job runs. A v1 port keeps file-backed spend classes consistent with the store.
contexts.name: spend-and-pricing

contexts.api_surface: Consumes /api/events/stream (SSE) and posts the Firebase ID token to the gt_session cookie bridge. Server action bellJobs reads jobs plus ledger seq.
contexts.description: The chrome that wraps every (studio) page. It has the header (nav sections, NEXT pile, 24h spend, ledger delta), the session handoff, the toast queue, the job bell and the live re-read feed. The server half reads kernel events and v1 live work once per request (facts.ts, headerFacts.ts, live.ts). The client half owns the Firebase session cookie bridge, the keymap, layer and toast residents, and the registered browser-storage keys. Records link to the routes that render them through links.ts, and the bell projects the same job rows Runs draws.
contexts.name: studio-shell

contexts.api_surface: Style port contract; server actions
contexts.description: The style detail page at library/style/[id], where a single extracted style is inspected and worked on in an Atelier with a Dossier. Its own port holds the contract, schema, wire format and fixture data and acts, switching between fixture and real sides, and actions apply changes to the style.
contexts.name: style-atelier

contexts.api_surface: Style read/write/export
contexts.description: The kernel's style store: schema, writers, driver and the export that regenerates styles.json, with v1 and v1 theme adapters for legacy style data.
contexts.name: style-store

contexts.description: Visual style locking and picture culling: style slots, facts, trial matrix, proof sheet and lock gate, with cull tiles, cut review and blind pair comparison. Operators pick, cull and lock styles from rendered trials.
contexts.name: style-trials-cull

contexts.api_surface: Suno vendor driver
contexts.description: Drives Suno song generation through pluggable drivers (real and fake), with proposal drafting, a job queue, a library of results and a store. A CLI runs the flow unattended.
contexts.name: suno-driver-queue

contexts.api_surface: Consumed by app/api/turns/preview (duration median from the stats ring); outbound calls to the Claude CLI and the Google generative API; optional LIGHTTRACK_URL usage events
contexts.description: The single chokepoint for every LLM reasoning call in the app. The router walks a capability-, transport- and key-aware provider chain (Claude CLI, Google) with no silent eliminations, and a repair turn hands a validator-rejected answer back to the model with the exact failing paths. Each settled turn feeds a console log, a bounded duration/cost stats ring for dispatch previews, an opt-in LightTrack usage sink, and a count-only text-usd spend ledger (it books vendor-reported cost and never refuses a turn).
contexts.name: text-reasoning-engine

contexts.description: Plans, cuts and reports on trailer structure for a script. It reads the script into structure types, applies thresholds and operations, produces a cut plan and notes, and reports findings. It runs the rule set in trailer/rules and feeds the script gate.
contexts.name: trailer-structure-engine

contexts.description: The individual dramaturgy rules a trailer is checked against: cards, connectors, cues, escalation, graph, ladder, magnitude, promises, reset, spine and withholding. Each rule inspects the structured trailer and emits findings the engine collects.
contexts.name: trailer-structure-rules

contexts.description: Interactive @gt/ui primitives and shared plumbing: button, toggle, segmented control, field, tab rail, fold, panel, toast and level sheet, plus cx, vars and the CSS-module typings. Every route builds its forms and chrome from these.
contexts.name: ui-controls-shell

contexts.description: Ledger-facing and time-based shapes: breadcrumbs, header chips, event rows with usd formatting, ledger links, JSON highlighting, time strip and waveform. Also holds INVENTORY.md, the map from each shape to its prototype source.
contexts.name: ui-ledger-timeline

contexts.description: The non-prose vocabulary that replaces narration: chip, ghost, glyph, hint (held to the twelve-word rule), caps heading, empty state, error line, keycaps, stale badge and the sr-only a11y channel.
contexts.name: ui-marks-and-text

contexts.description: State and origin shapes: status pill, tally, pip row, stack bar, facts, facet row, provenance, source tag, upstream break, consequence panel and channel badge. They show where a thing came from, how it stands and what an action would cost.
contexts.name: ui-status-provenance

contexts.api_surface: Backs the /api/import route (preview and commit) and the archive export download.
contexts.description: Brings v1 Gravitone data into the kernel store and exports it again. It reads and writes the `.gravitone` NDJSON archive in v1's byte format, stages a v1 project or shelf (items, themes) as a reviewable preview, then commits it in one transaction with its picture bytes moved into the blob store. It also imports pre-job-system runs (forge, extract, Dojo, strips, article, music-video, Suno) as Run rows with terminal jobs, and re-exports a kernel project as an archive that v1 can read back.
contexts.name: v1-import-and-archive

contexts.api_surface: Route(job) to vendor/model
contexts.description: Chooses which vendor and model serves a job: routing tables, posture, reserve and route logic, with calibration series that tune expectations from measured outcomes. Feeds spend quotes and job dispatch.
contexts.name: vendor-routing-and-calibration

contexts.api_surface: Producer definitions registered with the kernel
contexts.description: Producers for the visual side of a piece: frames and their look, stills, motion, style, strips, extraction and cuts. Each is a producer definition with plans or units that the kernel prices and runs. Outputs feed music-video assembly.
contexts.name: visual-producers

use_cases.description: A creator organises promoted image plates into a folder tree with drag-and-drop and bulk operations, previews them in a lightbox, and makes individual plates available across all their projects.
use_cases.name: Asset Library Management

use_cases.description: An operator evaluates whether a generated character's visual identity holds across camera setups and across time within a clip using FaceNet/DINOv2 similarity anchored to film ground-truth floor and ceiling values.
use_cases.name: Character Visual Consistency

use_cases.description: A creator walks a project through all five steps—Research, Script, Frames, Score, Cut—in a guided stepper that persists state locally in IndexedDB and calls AI services at each step.
use_cases.name: Content Production Pipeline

use_cases.description: A developer or designer inspects the live design-guideline viewer—Identity, Law, Parts, and Migration tabs—to verify component compliance and surface gaps before shipping a new UI surface.
use_cases.name: Design System Kit

use_cases.description: Operators run a mass-generation forge that crosses scenes against style recipes, then evaluate whether a named technique improves style fidelity over a baseline in the dojo A/B harness, before promoting winners to the curated catalogue.
use_cases.name: Foundry Style Training

use_cases.description: Script beats are decomposed into scene specs by an AI director pass, then routed to an image vendor (Imagen, Leonardo, Qwen, or Ollama) to produce visual plates assembled in an Assembly ledger and compared in an Alternatives contact-sheet.
use_cases.name: Frame Plate Generation

use_cases.description: A creator places cues against picture on a clock-based spotting surface; ElevenLabs generates audio from a CueBrief whose durations are derived from picture timings; takes land in the Audio Workbench for review.
use_cases.name: Music Cue Scoring

use_cases.description: A creator interactively experiments with all four ElevenLabs generation modes—cue generation, free plan drafting, composition, and inpainting—outside the main pipeline to prototype a sound direction before committing to scoring.
use_cases.name: Music Playground

use_cases.description: A creator views all their projects in a progress matrix, reads per-phase status across five columns, and creates, edits, or deletes projects from the shelf.
use_cases.name: Project Shelf & Progress

use_cases.description: A persistent background research job builds a triage notebook of facts and unknowns; the creator scopes decisions across the board; the pipeline condenses findings into a craft-grounded, beat-checked script.
use_cases.name: Research-to-Script Generation

use_cases.description: A creator authors a trailer-discipline script with beat-level editing, energy curves, connector picks, and movement sections—a structurally distinct Step 2 branch that enforces trailer beat law independently of the educational script path.
use_cases.name: Trailer Script Editing

use_cases.description: A creator generates image candidates in the Foundry, curates them in the keyboard-navigated cull grid, runs a five-beat proof trial in the Library Atelier, and locks a visual identity that gates all subsequent project work.
use_cases.name: Visual Style Locking
